name: Turbo engine carrier (Motortraeger)
description: Cross member carrying the 993 Turbo powertrain, part number 993 115 021 53. The PET catalogue places it in illustrated group 109-00 "Engine suspension Turbo", position 17: the Turbo application is established, not inferred. Structural part carrying the engine mass and its dynamic loads into the body shell.

classification.intended_use: Supports the powertrain and transmits its loads to the body shell

known_limits: Part presumed critical by SAFETY.md: main mounting of the powertrain.
Neither the part nor the instruments are available: the record cannot go beyond concept status, since no measurement is possible.
The PET distinguishes three 993 carriers: -90 standard (Carrera, C4, S, 4S), -41 RS, -53 Turbo. They are not interchangeable without proof, and no dimension currently allows them to be compared.
No known replacement alternative for the Turbo carrier: the tubular carrier from the specialist market is explicitly non-Turbo.
Price transcribed from the vendor product page: 1,788 USD excluding shipping, availability "available soon". The 225 to 270 EUR figure previously reported by a research summary was wrong.
Original material, mass and price remain unknown, including in the PET transcription: the catalogue does not publish them.

Failure mode established at the level of the 964 family, not on this part number: the part cracks, is repaired by welding and commonly receives an added reinforcement (SRC-PCGB-CRACKED-ENGINE-MOUNT-BRACKET, SRC-PFF-RENNLINE-MOTORTRAEGER, pages read). Welding a reinforcing gusset can warp the part. A "slightly reinforced" factory revision from about 1991 is mentioned with no supporting reference.
Corrosion documented on the 993 at the rear powertrain mounts and the rear side rails (911uk forum, page read): the environment of the part is corrosive.

Load case partly populated: a weighed engine mass is available, about 195 kg for a complete 993 twin-turbo unit without gearbox, but the fraction carried by this carrier rather than by the gearbox mount remains unknown, as do the center of gravity position and the lever arm of the engine torque.
Carrera engine torque of 330 Nm at 5,000 rpm used for lack of better data; the higher Turbo value has not been transcribed.
A polymer print of this part can only serve to check interfaces, never to carry the engine.

Titanium trade-off settled by the claimed mass: at a claimed 1.96 kg, the gain at equal stiffness would be about 0.45 kg, or 0.03 percent of the vehicle mass, against a full engineering review, a process qualification and non-destructive testing. Titanium is not justified on this part as it stands. The defect observed on the family is cracking, not mass.
No release possible before a formal engineering review and an approved validation plan.

Torques: 85 Nm on M12 for carrier to engine mount, confirmed by the group 10 factory table. The second figure reported, 45 to 50 Nm, does not appear in that table; the nearby value of 46 Nm concerns the gearbox mount to body shell. No carrier to body shell torque has been found.

The 1.96 kg mass and the 600 x 50 x 50 mm envelope come from the vendor product page. The length matches the proportions visible in the photographs: these values probably describe the part, rounded to the centimeter, and not a parcel. They remain claimed, not measured.

Open contradiction on the Turbo engine mass: 268 kg claimed with no stated scope against 195 kg weighed on a surface plate for a complete GT2 Race unit without gearbox. A 73 kg gap, of the same order as a gearbox. Not settled.

Construction observed on vendor photographs: one-piece part shaped as a curved blade of variable section, two large lightening holes, a cylindrical boss at each end. Nothing indicates a welded construction. The welded reinforcements mentioned on forums are therefore additions to a one-piece part, which remains consistent with the observed warping.

Metal additive manufacturing ruled out for this part: 600 mm does not fit in a common 250 x 250 x 325 mm LPBF build volume, the geometry calls for no additive advantage, and the observed failure mode is cracking, while as-built material loses on the order of 25 percent of endurance limit compared with the factory or wrought condition. Additive manufacturing remains relevant for an added reinforcement and for the polymer prototype.

Material choice framed but not settled, see evidence/material-options.md: since all steels have the same modulus, a stronger grade does not change the stiffness, and a stronger grade is more notch-sensitive. Weight reduction by substitution is ruled out, since aluminum has no endurance limit and is three times less stiff. The only defensible weight reduction goes through shape, and therefore through the load cases.

The workshop manual publishes no tightening torque for the carrier on the body shell, checked in the group 10 tables of the Carrera and Carrera 4 volumes. The reassembly procedure does, however, require all mounting nuts to be replaced.

Market cross-check: a tubular replacement carrier claims 0.635 kg of gain over an original carrier that is already gusseted, and is sold on strength, not mass. Confirms that the useful lever is durability. All these offers are non-Turbo.
